content.text:
Here is what was going wrong.

**Cause:** `getServerEnv()` in `src/env.ts` requires `DATABASE_URL` on `process.env`. The DB layer (`src/db/index.ts`) is fine without it because it uses the same default URL as the Makefile. So you could get a misleading situation: Postgres URL is effectively the default, but `make run-history-live` never set `DATABASE_URL`, so the first live-only path that calls `getServerEnv()` (building `GeminiCaseExtractor` with `GeminiService`) threw the Zod error.

**Fix:** Align `run-history-live` (and `run-history-mock`) with `run-initial-live` / `run-initial-mock` by passing `DATABASE_URL=$(DATABASE_URL)`. Make already defines `DATABASE_URL ?= postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5433/buena`, so `make run-history-live` now injects that into the `pnpm` process even when `.env` omits `DATABASE_URL`.

```76:80:/Users/gerograms/workspace/hackathon/Makefile
run-history-live:
	DATABASE_URL=$(DATABASE_URL) HISTORY_MODE=live HISTORY_DAY=$(DAY) pnpm run dry-run:history

run-history-mock:
	DATABASE_URL=$(DATABASE_URL) HISTORY_MODE=mock HISTORY_DAY=$(DAY) pnpm run dry-run:history
```

If you run `pnpm run dry-run:history` **without** Make, you still need `DATABASE_URL` in `.env` / `.env.local` (or in the shell) for live mode; that matches how `dry-run:baseline` is usually invoked.

[REDACTED]

<user_query>
Ah so it was my bad? I just broke it because it was writing to the DB?
</user_query>

Not really “your bad,” and you didn’t interrupt a DB write in progress.

By the time you saw **Days processed: 10** and the conflict log line, `runPropertyHistoryReplay` had already finished: each day is awaited in order, and those summaries print **after** that `await` returns. So the work for all 10 days was already committed; Postgres wasn’t still flushing that replay when you hit Ctrl+C.

Exit **130** is just **SIGINT** (Ctrl+C). What usually happens here is: the script is **done**, but Node stays alive because the **Postgres client** keeps the event loop open. So it looks “stuck” even though nothing important is left to do—you’re not breaking an in-flight write, you’re stopping a process that forgot to close the pool.

So: **data from that run should be fine**; you only forced the process to quit instead of waiting for it to idle forever (or until we close the client—`queryClient.end()` in `dryRunHistory.ts` is meant to fix that clean exit).
